official_scope: disease, injury, health, and disability in populations
design_notes: Expanded seven locked topics into atomic concepts for clinic, learning guide, MCQ, and binder audit use. Concept counts vary by topic (10–14) based on tested skill density. No thin stubs; no duplicate concepts across topics. Surveillance attributes, outbreak data displays, association measures, causal criteria, frequency calculations, and prevention planning remain separate as intended by the original topic split.

topics.title: Epidemiologic foundations and population health approach

concepts.title: Epidemiology definition and population health purpose
concepts.description: Define epidemiology as the study of distribution and determinants of health-related states in populations and explain its application to disease, injury, and disability control.

concepts.title: Distinguish clinical medicine from public health approach
concepts.description: Contrast individual patient diagnosis and treatment with population-level prevention, data collection, and community intervention.

concepts.title: Describe the natural history and stages of disease
concepts.description: Identify the stages from susceptibility through subclinical, clinical, and recovery, disability, or death, and explain where prevention opportunities occur.

concepts.title: Interpret the spectrum of disease severity
concepts.description: Distinguish inapparent, mild, severe, and fatal cases and explain how case detection bias affects reported disease rates.

concepts.title: Differentiate infectious and noninfectious causes of disease
concepts.description: Classify health conditions by infectious agents, environmental/chemical causes, injuries, genetic conditions, and multifactorial causes.

concepts.title: Define endemic, epidemic, pandemic, outbreak, and cluster
concepts.description: Apply CDC terms for disease occurrence levels and distinguish outbreak from cluster and epidemic from pandemic using time, place, and expected baseline.

concepts.title: Explain John Snow's cholera outbreak investigation
concepts.description: Describe how John Snow used descriptive mapping, water supply comparison, and removal of the Broad Street pump to identify cholera transmission and found modern field epidemiology.

concepts.title: Apply the epidemiologic approach to solving health problems
concepts.description: List and apply the core steps: confirm problem, describe by person place time, analyze risk factors, implement control, and evaluate.

concepts.title: Describe population health including injury and disability
concepts.description: Explain how population health measures include disease, injury, disability, and quality of life outcomes, not only infections.

concepts.title: Define core epidemiologic vocabulary from CDC Principles
concepts.description: Distinguish determinants, risk factors, protective factors, exposure, outcome, and control measures using CDC glossary definitions.

concepts.title: Define public health surveillance and its purposes
concepts.description: Explain surveillance as ongoing systematic collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of health data for action.

concepts.title: Apply the five-step surveillance process
concepts.description: List and order the five steps: data collection, analysis, interpretation, dissemination, and linkage to action.

concepts.title: Evaluate passive surveillance systems
concepts.description: Describe passive surveillance where providers report on their own initiative and assess strengths, weaknesses, and common uses.

concepts.title: Evaluate active surveillance systems
concepts.description: Describe active surveillance where health agencies solicit reports and assess increased completeness, cost, and timeliness tradeoffs.

concepts.title: Evaluate sentinel surveillance systems
concepts.description: Describe sentinel surveillance using selected reporting sites or providers to monitor trends and detect changes in high-risk or representative populations.

concepts.title: Evaluate syndromic surveillance systems
concepts.description: Describe syndromic surveillance using prediagnostic clinical data or symptoms to detect outbreaks earlier than confirmed diagnosis.

concepts.title: Distinguish registry, survey, and vital statistics surveillance
concepts.description: Compare registry-based surveillance, population surveys, and vital statistics as different surveillance data sources and their typical uses.

concepts.title: Interpret sensitivity of a surveillance system
concepts.description: Explain sensitivity as the proportion of true health events detected and apply it to judge a system's ability to find cases.

concepts.title: Interpret positive predictive value of surveillance signals
concepts.description: Explain positive predictive value as the likelihood that reported or detected events are true cases, and evaluate false-positive burden.

concepts.title: Evaluate timeliness and data quality in surveillance
concepts.description: Assess timeliness from event onset to reporting and action, and describe completeness, accuracy, and representativeness as data quality attributes.

concepts.title: Detect and confirm an outbreak
concepts.description: Identify an outbreak as cases in excess of expected baseline and confirm through case verification, lab confirmation, and time-place clustering.

concepts.title: Order the steps of an outbreak investigation
concepts.description: List and apply the classic outbreak investigation steps: prepare, verify, define cases, describe, develop hypotheses, evaluate, implement control, communicate.

concepts.title: Construct an outbreak case definition
concepts.description: Create operational case definitions with person, place, time criteria and classify cases as confirmed, probable, or possible.

concepts.title: Describe cases by person, place, and time
concepts.description: Apply descriptive epidemiology to characterize outbreak cases by demographic features, geographic location, and time of onset.

concepts.title: Build and use a line list in outbreak investigations
concepts.description: Construct a line list with identifying, clinical, demographic, and exposure data for each case, and use it to generate descriptive findings.

concepts.title: Construct an epidemic curve
concepts.description: Create an epidemic curve by plotting case counts by date of onset and use it to estimate exposure period and outbreak timing.

concepts.title: Interpret epidemic curve patterns
concepts.description: Distinguish point source, continuous common source, and propagated outbreaks by epidemic curve shape and peak timing.

concepts.title: Interpret spot maps for spatial clustering
concepts.description: Use spot maps to identify geographic clustering of cases and generate hypotheses about sources or common exposures.

concepts.title: Interpret PFGE patterns in outbreak investigations
concepts.description: Compare pulsed-field gel electrophoresis banding patterns to identify genetically related isolates and link cases to a common source.

concepts.title: Interpret WGS/SNP clustering and PulseNet data
concepts.description: Use whole genome sequencing and SNP differences to determine transmission clusters and integrate PulseNet surveillance for outbreak detection.

topics.title: Epidemiologic study designs and association measures

concepts.title: Distinguish observational and experimental study designs
concepts.description: Classify epidemiologic studies as observational when exposure is not assigned or experimental when the investigator allocates interventions.

concepts.title: Design and interpret cross-sectional studies
concepts.description: Describe simultaneous measurement of exposure and outcome to estimate prevalence, and recognize inability to establish temporal sequence.

concepts.title: Design and interpret case-control studies
concepts.description: Compare exposure frequencies between cases and controls; explain retrospective direction, selection of controls, and odds ratio as the measure of association.

concepts.title: Design and interpret cohort studies
concepts.description: Follow exposure-defined groups over time to compare incident outcomes; explain prospective vs retrospective cohorts and risk ratio interpretation.

concepts.title: Design and interpret ecological studies
concepts.description: Analyze group-level exposure and outcome data to generate hypotheses, and recognize ecological fallacy limitations.

concepts.title: Design and interpret randomized controlled trials
concepts.description: Describe random allocation of intervention, blinding, placebo control, and use of risk measures to assess efficacy in trials.

concepts.title: Calculate attack rates in outbreaks
concepts.description: Compute attack rate as cases divided by exposed population and interpret risk of illness among exposed groups.

concepts.title: Calculate and interpret risk ratios
concepts.description: Compute risk ratio comparing incidence in exposed and unexposed groups and interpret strength and direction of association.

concepts.title: Calculate and interpret odds ratios
concepts.description: Compute odds ratio from 2x2 tables for case-control studies and interpret it as an estimate of exposure-disease association.

concepts.title: Calculate vaccine effectiveness and efficacy
concepts.description: Apply formulas using attack rates in vaccinated and unvaccinated or relative risk reduction to compute vaccine effectiveness/efficacy.

concepts.title: Interpret confidence intervals for association measures
concepts.description: Explain 95% confidence interval as range of plausible values, use null value inclusion to judge statistical significance, and assess precision.

concepts.title: Identify selection bias in epidemiologic studies
concepts.description: Recognize selection bias from differential participation, case/control selection, or loss to follow-up that distorts exposure-disease association.

concepts.title: Identify information bias in epidemiologic studies
concepts.description: Recognize misclassification, recall bias, and measurement error that distort exposure or outcome classification.

concepts.title: Identify confounding and control for it
concepts.description: Define confounding as mixing of effects by a third variable associated with exposure and outcome, and describe control methods such as randomization, restriction, matching, stratification, and adjustment.

concepts.title: Apply Bradford Hill criteria for causal inference
concepts.description: Evaluate causality using strength, consistency, specificity, temporality, biological gradient, plausibility, coherence, experiment, and analogy.

concepts.title: Apply Koch's postulates for infectious disease causation
concepts.description: List and apply Koch's postulates linking a specific microorganism to disease using isolation, culture, and transmission evidence.

concepts.title: Apply Evans' postulates for chronic disease causation
concepts.description: Use Evans' epidemiological postulates including exposure prevalence and prevalence/incidence relationships to support causation in noninfectious diseases.

concepts.title: Interpret directed acyclic graphs for causal relationships
concepts.description: Draw and interpret DAGs to show variables, causal arrows, confounding, mediators, and colliders without cycles.

concepts.title: Apply sufficient-component cause models
concepts.description: Explain sufficient causes, component causes, and necessary causes using pie diagrams for multifactorial disease causation.

concepts.title: Use GRADE framework for evidence certainty
concepts.description: Evaluate certainty of evidence across studies considering risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, and upgrade factors.

concepts.title: Apply the agent-host-environment triad
concepts.description: Analyze disease as interaction of agent characteristics, host susceptibility, and environmental conditions that bring them together.

concepts.title: Describe the chain of infection components
concepts.description: Identify pathogen, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host as links to interrupt.

concepts.title: Distinguish direct and indirect transmission modes
concepts.description: Classify transmission as direct contact, droplet, airborne, vehicle, vectorborne, and fomite, with examples and control implications.

concepts.title: Explain herd immunity and threshold calculation
concepts.description: Define herd immunity as population resistance, calculate threshold H = 1 - 1/R0, and explain implications for outbreak control.

concepts.title: Interpret R0 as basic reproduction number
concepts.description: Define R0 as average secondary cases from one infective in a fully susceptible population and use it to assess epidemic potential.

concepts.title: Interpret Re as effective reproduction number
concepts.description: Define Re as actual average secondary cases under current conditions with immunity and control measures; use Re > 1 or < 1 to assess epidemic trajectory.

concepts.title: Distinguish ratio, proportion, and rate
concepts.description: Calculate and distinguish ratios as division of unrelated or same quantities, proportions as part over whole, and rates as events over person-time.

concepts.title: Calculate point prevalence
concepts.description: Compute point prevalence as cases present at a specific time divided by total population at that time; interpret as disease burden.

concepts.title: Calculate period prevalence
concepts.description: Compute period prevalence as cases present anytime during a defined period divided by mid-period population.

concepts.title: Calculate cumulative incidence
concepts.description: Compute cumulative incidence as new cases over a defined period divided by disease-free population at start; interpret as average risk.

concepts.title: Calculate incidence rate with person-time
concepts.description: Compute incidence rate as new cases divided by total person-time at risk, and interpret units as cases per person-time.

concepts.title: Explain the relationship between prevalence and incidence
concepts.description: Apply the formula prevalence ≈ incidence × average duration to predict changes in prevalence with disease recovery or death.

concepts.title: Calculate and interpret crude mortality rate
concepts.description: Compute crude death rate as total deaths divided by total population per time period and explain its limitations for comparing populations.

concepts.title: Calculate and interpret case fatality rate
concepts.description: Compute case fatality rate as deaths from a disease divided by total cases, expressed as percent, and interpret severity.

concepts.title: Calculate cause-specific and proportionate mortality
concepts.description: Compute cause-specific mortality rates as deaths from a specific cause divided by population and proportionate mortality as cause deaths divided by total deaths; interpret each.

concepts.title: Calculate and interpret age-adjusted mortality rates
concepts.description: Apply direct or indirect standardization to remove age structure differences and compare mortality across populations with different age distributions.

concepts.title: Interpret line, bar, and scatter graphs in epidemiology
concepts.description: Choose and interpret line graphs for trends, bar charts for counts, and scatter plots for relationships between variables.

concepts.title: Read and critique epidemiologic data tables
concepts.description: Extract rates, counts, and percentages from tables; identify missing denominators, inconsistent units, and misleading comparisons.

concepts.title: Apply primary prevention strategies
concepts.description: Describe interventions to prevent disease before onset, including vaccination, sanitation, behavior change, and injury prevention.

concepts.title: Apply secondary prevention through screening
concepts.description: Identify screening and early detection to reduce disease progression, and evaluate screening criteria such as sensitivity and lead time.

concepts.title: Apply tertiary prevention and rehabilitation
concepts.description: Describe treatment, rehabilitation, and disability limitation after disease onset to reduce complications and improve function.

concepts.title: Distinguish disease control, elimination, and eradication
concepts.description: Differentiate control as reducing incidence to accepted level, elimination as zero cases in a geographic area, and eradication as permanent global zero cases.

concepts.title: Use isolation and quarantine in disease control
concepts.description: Distinguish isolation of sick individuals from quarantine of exposed well persons and apply based on transmission mode and incubation period.

concepts.title: Apply contact tracing in outbreak control
concepts.description: Identify and monitor contacts of cases, calculate monitoring periods, and explain interruption of transmission chains.

concepts.title: Evaluate environmental and vector control measures
concepts.description: Select sanitation, water treatment, vector reduction, and environmental modification strategies to interrupt transmission for specific diseases.

concepts.title: Evaluate vaccination programs as control strategies
concepts.description: Assess routine immunization, catch-up campaigns, and ring vaccination for outbreak containment; interpret coverage thresholds for prevention.

concepts.title: Use health promotion and risk communication in control
concepts.description: Design behavior change and risk communication messages to improve adoption of control measures during outbreaks and chronic disease prevention.

concepts.title: Critique pre/post intervention data and control measures
concepts.description: Compare disease frequency before and after interventions, account for secular trends and biases, and evaluate whether control strategies worked.

concepts.title: Propose a tailored prevention and control strategy set
concepts.description: Select primary, secondary, and tertiary interventions appropriate to a given scenario, target population, agent, and setting.
